correctionPolicy.reason: First-pass hard veto: visible neck termination seam and camera-dependent planar fluke collapse. The production-loop hard-veto rule requires immediate family retirement; scores are not averaged to waive this.

reference.authority: secondary-inferred; written build-contract governs anatomy and three wing fingers; no pixel-exact texture requirement

evidence.inspectionOrder: All actual orbit, clay, and pose pixels before implementation diagnosis.
evidence.scope: Anatomy and posed cross-view coherence only. Separate reviewer owns cinematic sequence, camera, and temporal proof.

Flat rear skull/neck boundary and broad cream neck termination; fluke collapses almost entirely edge-on.
Profile confirms abrupt skull collar, uniform straight extended neck, plugged-in rod shoulder; flat leaf tail blades.

hardVetoes.observation: Visible circumferential flat termination/step between straight neck sleeve and independently swept skull. Cream throat ends as a straight cut below the cheek. It survives clay and both sides.
hardVetoes.criterion: No visible seams/root slots; parent owns attachment socket; no duplicate collar.

hardVetoes.observation: Required tail fluke is thin leaf geometry: visible as two flat blades in profile but collapses to almost a line from top/45. Changing view determines whether the tail identity exists.
hardVetoes.criterion: No camera-dependent shapes, disappearing required forms, or flat-plane collapse; build-contract explicitly forbids flat fins disappearing in profile.

constructionDiagnosis.neck: Head sections are authored independently in seaDragonHeadGeometry; mission body ends using separate ring radius and extension (2.05*scaleZ) while skull position uses 2.30*scaleZ. Those unrelated end profiles and normals produce the photographed cut. Deepening overlap alone does not provide a shared tangent/section.
constructionDiagnosis.shoulder: addSeaDragonArticulatedWing builds a small tube/sphere shoulder then rigid elbow tubes. Whole group is positioned at points[6]; no body-surface skin transition follows local torso cross-section. Pixels show the resulting stump/rod insertion.
constructionDiagnosis.fluke: tailFinGeometry uses THREE.ShapeGeometry rotated into a single plane. This directly explains edge-on disappearance.
constructionDiagnosis.finSystem: Dorsal/cheek fins cannot be postponed wholesale as finish because they change the approved macro outline. Scales, fine whiskers, and eye polish may remain later.

nextFamilyProposal.hypothesis: Use a shared section/frame construction for continuous torso-neck-skull boundary, body-owned muscular shoulder roots consumed by articulated wing limbs, and a closed cambered fluke with finite cross-section. These are a genuinely different attachment/volume representation, not more collars layered over family1.
controls: Same target, cameras, orbit timestamps, global scale, gameplay API, and thresholds.
Keep successful long torso taper, continuous snout, modest eyes, curved horns, and three-finger scalloped membrane identity.
One source owns neck boundary section and normals, including cream throat continuity; animated head consumes that exact socket.
Build shoulder root volume from the local moving torso surface to the upper arm; preserve arm articulation without exposed root caps.
Replace planar tail leaves with closed cambered lobes sharing a tapered tail peduncle; retain silhouette in top, side, front/rear and fold poses.
Include macro dorsal/cheek fin masses before renewed macro gate; micro-detail follows approval.
requiredEvidence: Repeat all 18 unchanged studio images plus close neck/shoulder/fluke clay crops.
Add clear underside and neutral spread/fold frames if existing poses remain occluded.
Require every critical view/category >=.85; family2 has at most its own one bounded correction if no hard veto.

notes: No production code or cameras edited by reviewer.
This is a substantial improvement over baseline primitive head and sail wings, but improvement does not equal gate approval.
No animation, phone, final finish, or gameplay approval is implied.
